scope.flow: ServiceManager::registerAgents -> ServiceRegistry::registerAgents agent instance registration and the already-registered check
scope.environment: ServiceManager / ServiceRegistry agent instance registration with attacker-controlled fake services

entities.name: Alice's fake service with minimal bond
Legitimate service Bob intends to register to

statements.text: Bob owns an agent instance and intends to register it to a legitimate service.
Alice knows Bob's instance address before it is officially registered.
Alice creates a fake service with minimal bond requirements (e.g., 1 wei).
Bob's agent instance is not yet registered to another service at the time Alice acts.
Alice registers Bob's instance to her fake service and deploys it.
Bob attempts to register the same instance to the legitimate service.

ServiceRegistry::registerAgents checks that each agent instance is not already registered to another service, and this check can be exploited to prevent a legitimate instance from being registered to a valid service.
ServiceManager::registerAgents does not verify that the caller is the designated operator of each instance being registered.
ServiceManager::registerAgents should verify that the caller is the designated operator of each instance being registered, so that only authorized entities can register a given instance.
All agent instances expose an operator function or equivalent.
This check can be exploited by an attacker to prevent a legitimate instance from being registered to a valid service, effectively locking it indefinitely.
When Bob attempts to register the same instance to the legitimate service, the transaction fails due to the instance already being registered elsewhere.
Because Alice controls the fake service, she can keep it alive indefinitely, permanently blocking Bob from using his instance.
In cases where an agent instance holds funds and is non-upgradeable, being registered to a malicious service can render it permanently unusable
leading to a complete loss of those funds.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether Alice's registration call is permissionless; only that she knows the instance address.
The 'cannot be unbonded' and 'keep alive indefinitely' claims are described as consequences, not established preconditions.
No explicit statement that Bob's instance is unregistered at the exact moment of Alice's action beyond 'before it is officially registered'.
The operator-verification requirement is a recommended mitigation, not a stated existing property of the code.
